question: Do the geometry cutout fixes, router.java_quirks.octagon_box_cutout_branch3=false (branch 3 of IntOctagon::cutout_from_box trims the upper right octagon to the widened upper box, so the drill-page pieces no longer overlap) and router.java_quirks.simplex_prev_division_line=false (Simplex::cutout_from assigns its previous division line; inert by construction), each alone and both, keep the unrouted total within N02's totals rule (accept no-regress: correctness fixes) of Java's cutouts, with no via in a pad, no copper below the minimum and no new clearance or DRC error, and how often does a run reach the two branches?
noise_note: canary-pwr's band is routing-quality.md's 10; every other board's band is the totals rule's default max(2, ceil(5 % of connections)) from the record's connections
engine: freerouting-rs at the implementing commit (main b93bcd0 with N06.4's diff), one Linux release build for every arm; the default profile (enhanced, whose ENHANCED table does not touch java_quirks) and the default passes, so the arms differ only in the two router.java_quirks keys

baseline.engine: freerouting-rs at the implementing commit (main b93bcd0 with N06.4's diff), one Linux release build for every arm; the default profile (enhanced, whose ENHANCED table does not touch java_quirks) and the default passes, so the arms differ only in the two router.java_quirks keys
baseline.what: both keys set to true: Java's cutouts

simplex_prev_division_line.what: the simplex fix alone; inert by construction (Simplex::cutout_from_counted), so its sessions must equal the baseline's

all.what: candidate: batch G, both fixes; its sessions must equal octagon_box_cutout_branch3's

pairs_rule: the verdict pair is judged by the totals block with the hard and guard metrics below; the reported pairs are the switch-by-switch bisection (N06's decisions: one switch per bug), run up front. The simplex pair must show session_differences 0 on every row, and the all arm must give octagon_box_cutout_branch3's sessions byte for byte; either failing is a bug in N06.4's diff, not a verdict

boards.eligibility: every row; no row is dropped after a number. Chosen before any number: the four DSN fixtures of N06.10 and N06.11 (their hashes), which route with vias, so every pass reads drill pages; canary-pwr also goes through the KiCad plugin path (plugin_canary)

metric_definitions.via_in_pad: freerouting-dev gate collect's count on the imported SES; plugin canary: tools/kicad-oracle/via_in_pad.py
metric_definitions.below_minimum: the nets with copper under their class width in freerouting-dev widths <DSN> <SES> (under_mm > 0); plugin canary: KiCad track_width errors
metric_definitions.simplex_prev_division_line_reached: STATS total.counts.simplex_prev_division_line_reached; 0 by construction in every arm
metric_definitions.clearance_violations: the router's clearance violations of the final board (RESULT board_statistics; gate collect's clearance_violations)
metric_definitions.drc_real: plugin canary only: KiCad error-severity items other than unconnected items
metric_definitions.kicad_unconnected: plugin canary only: KiCad's unconnected items after the import (canary grade.sh); the totals signal where it is a number
metric_definitions.unrouted: gate collect's unrouted (connections.incomplete_count) of the final board; the totals signal of the DSN rows, which have no KiCad board
metric_definitions.session_differences: n06_run.py: 1 when the arm's SES differs from the baseline's
metric_definitions.octagon_box_cutout_branch3_reached: STATS total.counts.octagon_box_cutout_branch3_reached: the drill-page and tie-pin cutouts whose branch 3 changes a piece, counted in both arms

paired_rule_note: pass_rule is retained for gate parser validation; the registered verdict uses totals with accept=no-regress
keep_rule: N06's accept rule for (b) fixes: a batch is accepted when the hard guards hold, no board regresses by more than twice its noise band and the total is not worse than the set's noise; a neutral fix stays in. If the verdict pair passes, N06.13 turns octagon_box_cutout_branch3 off in ENHANCED through N05; simplex_prev_division_line changes nothing and is promoted or left by N06.13's decision on inert switches
accept: Unit and invariant tests pin both behaviours of both switches (tests/cutout_invariant.rs, box_cutout_branch3_switch_both_behaviours).
simplex_prev_division_line_reached = 0 in every run, and the simplex arm's sessions equal the baseline's.
The verdict pair passes the totals rule (no-regress) with the hard and guard metrics.
Grade canary-pwr through the KiCad plugin path; no new real DRC, via-in-pad or below-minimum errors.
stop_rule: one registered run per arm per board; no reruns with other settings. No heavy run by the implementer.
orchestrator: Build the release CLI in the worktree with CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=2 CARGO_TARGET_DIR=target/orchestrator/n06-target; run orchestrator_command (it exits non-zero when sessions differ, which is expected for this batch, after writing summary.json with every run's counters); then grade each SES with gate collect and freerouting-dev widths, and judge the pairs with freerouting-dev gate --rule totals
orchestrator_command: CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=2 CARGO_TARGET_DIR=target/orchestrator/n06-target cargo build --release -p freerouting-cli && python3 tools/bench/n06_run.py docs/roadmap/prereg/N06.4.json --out target/orchestrator/n06-g
corpus_counter_command: N06_CUTOUT_COUNTERS_OUT=<absolute path>/n06-g-corpus.json CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=2 CARGO_TARGET_DIR=target/orchestrator/n06-target cargo test --release -p freerouting --test n06_cutout_reach unwired_area_splits_corpus_inventory -- --ignored --test-threads=1
corpus_counter_note: read-only: how often the search trees' area and outline-keepout splits, which keep Java's code in every arm, reach the two branches per corpus board. A nonzero branch-3 count on a registered board means the arms measure the drill pages only there

plugin_canary.source: canary-pwr-rev1.0, the original KiCad project at canary 9511d9a; supplied by the orchestrator; never edit the source project
plugin_canary.route: For each registered arm, run the release CLI on the plugin-exported DSN with the generated <stem>.args.json args verbatim, then the arm's explicit --router.java_quirks.* flags, --stats json --stats-out <arm>/stats.json and --result-json=<arm>/result.json. The same exported input serves every arm
plugin_canary.grade: canary grade.sh steps (ses_import.py, kicad-cli pcb drc --schematic-parity --refill-zones --severity-all, via_in_pad.py, inner_tracks.py); kicad_unconnected joins canary-pwr's row of the totals; no new real DRC, via-in-pad or below-minimum error

not_registered: the A14 exact set: legacy keeps both keys true, so A14 is unaffected
the search trees' area and outline-keepout splits: they keep Java's code in every arm (corpus_counter_command says where that matters)
seen_before_registration: only N06.4's unit and invariant tests: on fixtures/Issue269-min_fr_test (not a row), pass 1 reaches branch 3 7 times in both arms and the simplex merge 0 times (tests/n06_cutout_reach.rs). No routed number of any registered row, under any arm

decision_table.pass: N06.4's measurement [x]; N06.13 turns octagon_box_cutout_branch3 off in ENHANCED (N05) with its DIVERGENCES 'Profile enhanced' line
decision_table.fail: octagon_box_cutout_branch3 stays true in both profiles, with these numbers in N06.4 and N06.13

amendments.reason: main moved on before any N06.4 route (N06.5, N06.6, N06.7, N06.8, N06.12 and Q16.5 were committed after b93bcd0), and a check of the hard guards before any number found one the baseline arm breaks by design: below_minimum on a DSN row is defined as the nets with copper under their class width (freerouting-dev widths, under_mm > 0), which counts every trace narrower than its layer's class width, the steps of a neck-down taper included (quality/neckdown/width_report.rs), while every arm runs the default profile enhanced with neck_width_um = 300; canary-pwr-9511d9a.dsn has 300 and 400 um classes above its 200 um narrowest, so Java's cutouts would breach that hard limit wherever a taper is drawn (Q16.4's and Q10.4's failure mode). The other three DSN rows have one class width each. Written before any route of N06.4
amendments.changes: (1) engine base moved from main b93bcd0 with N06.4's diff to main 3b1bde6 (N06.4's diff committed as 5607634). Every java_quirks switch added since defaults to true (Java) and ENHANCED is unchanged (power_layer_traces=none, neck_width_um=300, via_clearance=net_class), so the arms still differ only in the two keys. The arms' engine, settings and command texts are unchanged; the command's relative binary path is resolved from the worktree root. (2) below_minimum, option (a), each board's own minimum: on a DSN row it is the number of delivered traces narrower than the board's narrowest class width (width_report::narrowest_class_width; the arms pass no min_trace_width floor) on the imported SES, minus those already in the input board; the nets under their class width (widths' under_mm > 0) are reported as below_class_width_nets, not judged. On the plugin row it stays KiCad's track_width errors against the Board Setup minimum. (3) via_in_pad, option (b), no new breach versus baseline: no number of any registered row under enhanced exists for the three small DSN rows (Q10.4's enhanced runs of canary-pwr-9511d9a.dsn, engine f6e75ab, had 0 in every arm), so to keep a breach Java's cutouts already make from deciding the verdict, an arm's via_in_pad is its count (gate collect's via_in_pad_count on the imported SES minus the input's; on the plugin row via_in_pad.py) minus the baseline arm's count on the same row, floored at 0; the raw counts are reported as via_in_pad_raw. The gate keeps both as hard metrics. (4) Records: the canary-pwr row carries the plugin row's kicad_unconnected and drc_real (its signal is kicad_unconnected, as registered) and the DSN route's other metrics; every row carries connections (board_statistics connections.total_count) for the default bands. simplex_prev_division_line_reached, the boards, the arms, the rule and the accept list unchanged

amendments.reason: written before any route of N06.4, after two findings. (i) N06.7's registered run (profile legacy, same engine; Issue026, bm08 and Issue676 are rows of both batches) graded with amendment 1's below_minimum definition gave 37 traces under the narrowest class width on Issue026's baseline session and 11 on bm08's: the router's pin neck-down (a trace entering a pad narrower than its width is drawn at the pad's width) puts copper under every class width by design, so the baseline arm would break amendment 1's hard limit too. (ii) main 4885a30 found that importing an SES into a clone of the input repeats the input's unfixed and user-fixed items (the SES saves them again), so after-minus-before counts in-pad input vias twice; Issue676's input has 48 unfixed wires and 6 unfixed vias (the import of its baseline session holds 12 vias where the router's board has 6)
amendments.changes: (1) below_minimum, option (b), no new breach versus baseline, replacing amendment 1's (2): on a DSN row an arm's below_minimum is the number of its delivered traces narrower than the board's narrowest class width that the input board does not already have (same layer, half width, nets and end corners), minus the baseline arm's number on the same row, floored at 0; the raw count is reported as below_minimum_raw and the nets under their class width as below_class_width_nets, neither judged. On the plugin row it is KiCad's track_width error count minus the baseline arm's, floored at 0 (raw reported). (2) via_in_pad keeps amendment 1's option (b), counted as main 4885a30's added_via_in_pad: a via in an SMD pad counts only when the input has no via with its centre, padstack and nets. (3) unrouted, clearance_violations, vias, length_mm and connections come from the router's own result manifest (board_statistics: connections.incomplete_count and maximum_count, clearance_violations.total_count, vias.total_count, traces.total_length_mm), not from an imported copy. simplex_prev_division_line_reached, the boards, the arms, the rule and the accept list unchanged
